title: What worked when getting Claude Code to handle stunt physics: flips, landings and wall-driving roads
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
Browser based stunt racer on sky roads hanging from balloons, with Claude Code. Stunt physics is easy to get wrong, so here’s the workflow that helped:

1. **One road, one car first.** All the early feedback was about how driving felt, before any tracks existed.
2. **Separate the air from the ground.** Flips and spins got their own controls in the air. Then came a landing check, where clean landings give a speed burst and clean flips fill nitro. Describing exactly what a bad landing looked like got better fixes than “landings feel off”.
3. **Test track pieces alone.** Ramps, loops, banked turns and gaps were each tuned on their own before being combined into full tracks.
4. **Hardest ask last.** Magnetic night roads that let you drive up walls and through corkscrews needed the car to stick to the road without breaking the normal driving. Doing it after everything else was stable made it much easier to debug.
5. **Respawn early in testing.** Falling off drops you back at the last checkpoint, which also made testing much faster.

It ended up with 12 tracks over dawn, noon, sunset and night, plus three cars and three bikes.
